THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FURTHER HEARING, THIS DAY,
 THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC-K:912  CRL.A No. 200002 of 2017  JUDGMENT

This appeal under Section 374 of Cr.PC is filed challenging the judgment of conviction and order dated 27.10.2016, by which, the accused herein is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 304 Part 1 of IPC and sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for ten years and to pay a fine of Rs.20,000/- and in default, to undergo further simple imprisonment for a period of six months.

2. The case of the prosecution in brief is as follows:
i) The marriage of the accused was performed with the victim, Shabhana, who is daughter of CW1 about eight years back, and since four years, the accused by doubting on the chastity of the said victim-Shabhana, subjected her to physical and mental cruelty and harassed her over trivial issues, and in spite of advise, the accused continued to do so, and the deceased, unable to bear the cruelty, returned to her parental home.
ii) On 10.5.2015, the accused came to the house of CW1 and by giving assurance to CW1, took back the deceased to his house.

On 20.5.2015 at 7.00 p.m., the accused caught hold the tuft of the deceased and banged her head to the wall and other parts of the body with force, due to which, the deceased fell down with bleeding injuries on her head and breathed her last.
The police, after the investigation, submitted the charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 302 of IPC.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:912 The learned Sessions Judge framed the charge against the accused for the aforesaid offences, and the same was read over and explained to the accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
3. The prosecution to prove its case, examined 21 witnesses as PWs.1 to 21 and marked 17 documents as Exs.P1 to P17(a) along with two material objects as MOs.1 and 2.

The accused got marked the document as Ex.D1.

sentences.text:
After the evidence of prosecution was concluded, the incriminating circumstances found in the evidence of prosecution witnesses were put to the accused as contemplated under Section 313(1)(b)
of Cr.PC, and the accused denied the said incriminating circumstances and stated that he had given a single blow to the deceased with his fist due to which she fell down and succumbed.

5. The learned Sessions Judge, after examining the material evidence on record, and also the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, framed the points for consideration, and recorded a finding that the death of Shabhana was homicidal, and that the prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused for the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC, however,
recorded a finding that, the accused is guilty of the offence punishable under Section 304 Part(1) of IPC.
Taking exception of the same, the accused is before this Court.

The learned counsel for the appellant submits that, taking into account the statement of accused recorded under section 313, and also in the absence of any direct evidence, the impugned judgment of conviction based only on the evidence of hear say witnesses is not sustainable in law.

7. The learned High Court Government Pleader for the State would submit that, the material evidence on record clearly indicates that, the homicidal death was caused due to the assault made by the accused, and the same is supported by corroborative material, and in the absence of any perversity or arbitrariness in the findings recorded by the learned Sessions Judge, the impugned judgment of conviction does not warrant any interference.
8. Considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
9.
PW1 is the mother of the deceased.
PWs.2 to 4 are the sisters of the deceased.
PWs.5 to 7 are the brothers of the deceased.
PW8 is the cousin of the deceased.
The said witnesses are the hear say witnesses, who have deposed on oath on the basis of the information furnished by the eye witness viz: PW12.
The said witnesses have not supported the case of the prosecution and nothing was elicited in their cross- examination to disbelieve their statement.
10. PW9 is the scribe of the complaint who has supported the case of the prosecution.

PWs.10 and 11 are the neighbours and witnesses to the spot, inquest and seizure mahazars and have not supported the case of the prosecution and were treated as hostile and nothing was elicited in their cross-examination to disbelieve their statement.
12.

PW12 is the eye witness to the incident and on the basis of the information furnished by him,
PW1 lodged the FIR, however, PW12 was treated as hostile and in his cross- examination, nothing was elicited.

sentences.text: 13. PW13 is the witness to the spot, inquest and seizure mahazars and has not supported the case of the prosecution and was treated as hostile.
14. PW14 is the mother of the accused and was treated as hostile.
15. PW15 is the panch witness to the spot panchanama and has not supported the case of the prosecution.
16. PW16 is said to have prepared the map of the place of incident and has supported the case of the prosecution.
17. PW17 is the Police Inspector, who conducted the investigation and laid the charge sheet and he supported the case of the prosecution.
18. PW18 is said to have shown the place of incident for drawing the map.
PW19 is the Police Inspector, who has recorded the FIR.
20. PW20 is the doctor, who has furnished the postmortem report, wherein he had opined that, the death was caused due to hemorrhage shock due to injury sustained to head.

In the cross-examination, PW20 stated that, if a person falls in a bathroom, and if his head comes in contact with hard object, there is possibility of sustaining head injury which is stated in the said postmortem report and it can cause death.
21. The incriminating circumstances were put to the accused as contemplated under Section 313 of Cr.PC.

In the said statement, the accused has stated that, after returning from mosque, a quarrel took place and he gave a single blow to the deceased with his hands due to which, she fell down and succumbed.
Admittedly, the eye witness, PW12 has turned hostile and the case of the prosecution revolves around the circumstantial evidence.
The postmortem report indicates that, the death was due to hemorrhage shock due to injury sustained to head.
The accused has categorically admitted in the 313 statement that, he had hit the deceased with his fist due to which she fell down and succumbed.

22. The learned Sessions Judge has convicted the accused for the offence punishable under Section 304 Part (I) of IPC, primarily, relying on the evidence of hearsay witnesses i.e., PWs.1 to 8 and the first principle of law is that, the NC: 2023:KHC-K:912 hearsay evidence is not inadmissible in law,
unless it is supported by corroborative material.
23.
The accused in his evidence has categorically stated that due to provocation, he hit the deceased due to which, she fell down and succumbed, which falls under Section 304 Part II of IPC.
PW12 has turned hostile and the evidence of PWs.1 to 8 is inadmissible in law.

Taking into consideration the 313 statement of the accused, the death of the deceased was due to single blow given by the accused,

sentences.text: and the act committed is without any intention to cause death, which does not constitute an offence punishable under section 304 Part I of IPC.
The accused has already undergone imprisonment for a period of more than eight years.

24. Section 304 Part II of IPC contemplates that, punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years or with fine or with both if the act is done with the knowledge that it is likely to cause death, but without any intention to cause death, or to cause such bodily injury as is likely to cause death.
The imprisonment for ten years if the act is one with the knowledge i.e. likely to cause death, but without any intention to cause death.

In the instant case, though the accused was aware that, his act is likely to cause death, but however, the prosecution has failed to prove that the accused had an intention to cause death of the deceased.
The accused was referred to NIMHANS, Bengaluru, to examine whether he was unsound mind or not.
No material is forthcoming in the records to indicate that, the accused was examined by the NIMHANS, Bengaluru as to whether he was unsound mind or not.
26. The accused is in custody for more than eight years and it would suffice if he is sentenced to undergo imprisonment for the period which he has already undergone.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal appeal is allowed.
ii) The judgment of conviction and the order of sentence dated 27.10.2016 passed in SC No.80/2015 by the learned Sessions Judge, at Yadgir, is hereby modified by sentencing the appellant-accused for the offence punishable under Section 304(2) of IPC and not for the offence punishable under Section 304(1) of IPC.
iii) The appellant - accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Section 304(2) of IPC .
iv) The learned Sessions Judge is hereby directed to release the fine amount, if any,
which is deposited by the appellant.
The bail bonds executed, if any, stand canceled.
Sd/-
